topics.title: First steps
steps: Sign in with your administrator account. Open Overview to check CPU, memory, storage and uptime. Open Services to check hosting service health.
Use Websites → Add website to create a WordPress, WHMCS or regular PHP/HTML host. Select a compatible PHP version.
Point the domain A record to the server IP. Upload or install your application, then enable SSL when DNS resolves correctly.
Save credentials when first displayed. Keep an off-server backup before making major changes.

topics.title: Navigation and appearance
steps: Use the menu button to hide or show navigation. LiteCP always uses dark mode, including the file editor, regardless of your device's appearance settings.

Expand Settings with its sidebar arrow to show Administrator password, Administrator email, Time zone, Backup settings, Server hostname, DNS resolver and Reboot server. Click the arrow again to collapse the sub-tabs. Save each section separately. Backup retention and remote destinations are configured in Backup settings; create backups and view their history on Backups.
The top bar shows the OS, hostname and server IP. Refresh server data with the refresh icon.

Use Quick search below the sidebar logo, or press Ctrl+K / Command+K, to find features, settings, websites, databases and mailboxes. The shortcut opens navigation when it is hidden. Select a result or use the arrow keys and Enter to jump to it. Escape closes search. Search opens the relevant section without changing settings.
Use the Documentation tab at any time. Search this manual by feature name or task.

topics.title: Create and manage a website
steps: Click Add website, choose the application type, enter the domain and select PHP. Database and application cron options depend on the application.
WHMCS release selection restricts PHP choices. Application provisioning prepares hosting resources; it does not upload a licensed WHMCS distribution.
Click the domain name to open the live website in a new tab. Use the file-manager icon to manage its public directory.
Changing PHP restarts that site runtime. Verify the application afterwards. Cron runs only when enabled and supported for that application.

topics.title: Website cron jobs
steps: Open Websites and click the Cron jobs icon beside the required domain. Custom jobs are available for every website, including regular PHP/HTML hosts.

Enter an optional name, choose a common schedule or edit Minute, Hour, Day, Month and Weekday. Use numbers, *, lists, ranges and steps. Weekdays run from 0 (Sunday) to 7 (also Sunday). If both day-of-month and weekday are restricted, cron runs when either matches.

Enter a single-line shell command. Use full paths to executables; the displayed PHP CLI path matches the website's selected PHP runtime. PHP 7.3 container commands require separate runtime support and are not offered as a custom-job PHP shortcut.

Schedules use the server time zone shown in the popup. Commands start in the website document root and run as its isolated account, with that account's filesystem permissions. Output is discarded unless your command redirects it to a log file.

Click Create cron job to save. Use Edit to change it, Disable to pause future runs, or Remove and confirm to remove the schedule. Disabling or removing a job does not stop a command that is already running.

Built-in WordPress and WHMCS five-minute tasks remain separate. Avoid creating a duplicate custom task for the same application. Detaching a website pauses its custom schedules and retains the saved definitions.

topics.title: SSL and detaching
steps: Enable SSL after the domain points to this server and public HTTP validation is reachable. Review any error instead of repeatedly requesting certificates.
Detaching removes the managed hosting configuration but preserves website files and databases. Confirm the displayed scope before continuing.

topics.title: Enable a runtime and configure a website
steps: Open Application Hosting. Node.js, Python and Ruby are disabled independently by default. Enable only the language you require; enabling alone starts no application.
Create a dedicated Regular PHP/HTML website. Save its application configuration before uploading source through File Manager or FTPS. WordPress and WHMCS websites cannot be converted by this feature.

Enable SSL before starting the application. Choose Configure website, the website and runtime version, then enter the startup command and optional dependency setup command. Saving configuration immediately protects the website with a maintenance response until its application starts.
Use a production application server that listens on 0.0.0.0:8080. PORT=8080 and HOST=0.0.0.0 are supplied to the container. The application directory is /app.

Start downloads the selected official runtime image, optionally runs dependency setup, starts the container and switches Nginx only after the application listens. Review errors and logs if setup or startup fails.

topics.title: Operate and change versions
steps: Start resumes a stopped application. Stop interrupts application traffic but retains the proxy configuration. Disable website runtime stops it and keeps the website in maintenance mode so application source stays private, retaining uploaded files and runtime configuration.
Disable website runtime before editing the version or commands. Save the new configuration and Start again. Dependencies may need rebuilding for a new version.
Disable all websites using a language before switching off that hosting feature. Configurations and files remain retained.

Application containers run as the website UID/GID, with a read-only system filesystem, a writable application directory, no added capabilities, and limits of 256 MiB memory, 1 CPU and 128 processes. Ports are bound only to localhost and Nginx handles the public domain.
Container restart policy and podman-restart.service provide boot startup for deployed apps. This does not replace monitoring or guarantee application health after reboot.

Local MySQL can be reached through /run/mysqld/mysqld.sock when present. Configure a database driver with unix socket support, the managed database username and its password. Database credentials are not automatically injected.

Use trusted dependencies. Setup commands can modify application files. Slim runtime images do not include every native build dependency; prebuild dependencies compatible with the selected runtime when needed.
Do not place passwords or tokens in startup/setup commands because configuration is visible to panel administrators. Use application configuration files and protect them appropriately.
Application images and old stopped containers are retained; there is no automatic destructive cleanup. Use the dependency installer if Podman is unavailable.

topics.title: Browse and edit files
steps: Select the website. Use the folder tree, breadcrumb, back/forward/up buttons or address field to navigate inside its public root.
Search filters the current folder. Toggle hidden files, sorting, and list/grid view as needed. Select files to see details and actions.

Use New file, New folder or Upload. Uploads have no panel-imposed file-size or queue-count cap and are sent one file at a time; disk space, browser and connection timeouts still apply. Completed files remain if a later queued file fails. Open text files in the editor and save changes. Binary files require download and an appropriate local editor.
Select items to copy, move, rename, change permissions, compress, extract or download. Existing-path conflicts and unsafe archive paths may be rejected.

topics.title: Trash and fullscreen
steps: Trash allows recovery before permanent deletion. Restore items from View trash. Emptying Trash or permanently removing items is irreversible and requires confirmation.
Full screen expands only the file-manager workspace. Use Exit full screen or Escape to leave. Open dialogs may consume Escape first.
Use the least permissions your application needs. Do not grant world-writable permissions to resolve an ownership issue.

topics.title: Create, download or delete
steps: Click the website backup icon to open its popup. Choose Create backup and keep the page open until completion.
The outer website.zip contains public_html.zip and databases.zip. Hidden files and empty directories are included; SQL dumps cover databases registered to that website.
Download the completed backup. Delete removes only the selected generated backup and intermediate files after confirmation, preserving the live website and databases.
Links or special files stop backup generation. External/unregistered databases are not included. Use a maintenance window for a consistent snapshot of a busy application.

Manual ZIP backups are separate from Backups page TAR archives. In the website backup popup, use Upload and inspect for a downloaded manual ZIP, or Restore beside a saved backup. Select an empty target website for files and an empty managed database for each SQL dump. Restore the files and required databases separately, then update application credentials if target names differ. Only trusted LiteCP nested ZIPs are supported, up to 2 GiB uploaded and 8 GiB extracted. Existing live data is rejected rather than overwritten. Inspected stages are retained under Migration until explicitly removed.

topics.title: Connect to a website with FTPS
steps: Click the FTP accounts icon beside the website. Enter a unique lowercase username and strong password, then Create account.
In your FTP client choose explicit FTP over TLS, server IP or configured FTP hostname, port 21, the account username and password, and passive mode.
Each login is confined to the selected website public directory. It does not create a shell or SSH account.
Edit password changes credentials; usernames are not renamed. Remove blocks future logins while preserving files. Existing connections may last until disconnected.

The FTP service must be installed. TCP 21 and passive ports 50000–50049 must be permitted by server and cloud firewalls. A trusted certificate matching the FTP hostname is required for normal production certificate validation.

topics.title: Create and manage databases
steps: Create a database with a unique database name, username and strong password. Copy icons copy database names and usernames individually.
Password resets require updating every application that uses that account. Deleting a database and user is permanent; back up and confirm the displayed scope.
A website may have an associated managed database; standalone databases can be created independently.

topics.title: Open phpMyAdmin
steps: Click the database name. A new tab opens and signs into that selected database automatically using a dedicated restricted account.
Use Structure or Browse to inspect tables; SQL, Search, Import and Export provide standard database tools within the selected database privileges.
Application database passwords are not read or changed. Launch tickets work once and expire quickly. If launch expires or a tab is blocked, return to LiteCP and click again.
An active LiteCP session is required for subsequent requests. Large imports may exceed phpMyAdmin upload or execution limits; use supported server import tools.
Editing or dropping data in phpMyAdmin affects the live application immediately. Export before changes.

topics.title: Create a mailbox or alias
steps: Hosted website domains appear automatically in the mailbox domain selector. Creating the first mailbox enables local mail routing for that domain.
Use Add mail domain for an email-only domain with no website hosted here.
Choose the domain, local part, strong password and quota, then Create mailbox. Use the full email address as the mail-client username.
Aliases forward a locally hosted source address to a destination address. An alias is not a separate IMAP mailbox.

Password resets require updating mail clients. Removing a mailbox disables login while retaining stored Maildir messages. Disabling email hosting stops mail services, preserving accounts and messages.

topics.title: Mailbox login and configuration
steps: Use Log in beside the mailbox to open configured webmail in a new tab. Enter the mailbox password; panel sign-in is not automatic mailbox sign-in.
If webmail is unavailable, configure a public mail hostname with matching TLS and install the webmail component first.
Configuration shows the domain DNS records and mail client settings. Incoming IMAP uses 993 with SSL/TLS; outgoing SMTP uses 465 with SSL/TLS or 587 with STARTTLS and authentication.

topics.title: Publish the records
steps: Open DNS records beside a mail domain, or Configuration beside a mailbox. Copy the actual generated record values to your DNS provider. LiteCP does not edit public DNS.
Publish the mail-host A record and domain MX record. Merge authorized senders into one SPF TXT record; do not create two SPF records.
Publish the generated default._domainkey DKIM TXT record. A missing key or DKIM service must be corrected before signing can work.
Begin DMARC in monitoring mode. Create the report mailbox before enabling reports; review results before choosing quarantine or reject.
Ask the server provider to set PTR/reverse DNS to the public mail hostname. Verify forward/reverse DNS, trusted TLS and outbound TCP 25.
Authentication records improve deliverability but do not guarantee inbox placement. Reputation, message content, recipient policy and blocked ports also matter.

topics.title: Check and restart services
steps: Services shows the managed hosting stack status. Restart a selected service only when necessary; websites or mail clients may briefly disconnect.
Use Logs to inspect the offered service/application log targets. Refresh to read new entries and use the exact error message when investigating a failure.
A green service state is a point-in-time health result, not proof that every application or external connection is working.

topics.title: Run a standard backup
steps: Select a website and choose local storage or a configured remote destination. Create backup and wait for completion.
Standard backups use a different TAR archive format from website manual ZIP backups. Keep an independent off-server copy and test your restore procedure.
Open Settings → Backup settings and add a remote destination with its host, port, protocol, account, remote path and password. Prefer FTPS or SFTP over unencrypted FTP.
SFTP requires a verified SSH host-key fingerprint. Verify it through a trusted channel before saving it. Remote destination passwords are encrypted in panel storage.
Local backup retention applies to standard archives according to Settings → Backup settings. Remote retention is managed at the destination. Review a backup status before relying on a remote copy.

topics.title: Move a website from an archive
steps: Create an empty unused target website with a compatible PHP version.
Upload a compatible cPanel archive containing public_html or Plesk export containing httpdocs, then inspect it. Select the website root and optional SQL dump.
Import only into an empty target. SQL uses a restricted target user and an empty managed database. Update application paths and database credentials afterwards.
Verify the website before changing DNS. Files, databases and active applications require consistency planning.

topics.title: Capture a live cPanel or Plesk source
steps: Connect with Linux root SSH using a dedicated unencrypted private key or root password. LiteCP can detect the host key and ask you to trust its SHA256 fingerprint; verify it independently before accepting. Detection alone does not prove the server's identity. Password login must be enabled on the source; interactive MFA and Plesk for Windows are unsupported.
Discover and select a source account or subscription. Confirm native backup creation; source and destination require enough free disk space.
LiteCP retains the native archive, verifies the transfer checksum and stages compatible primary website files and SQL for review. Additional databases need separate target mapping.
Capture is not a complete account restore. Mail, DNS, SSL, addon sites, packages, reseller settings and arbitrary cron jobs are not automatically activated.
Archive size and extraction limits apply. Unsupported links/layouts need manual review. Source exports and retained backups are not automatically cleaned up.
Forget source credentials after capture and revoke the dedicated source key independently. Keep the source authoritative until all services are verified.

topics.title: Find and install modules
steps: Use Search extensions, select a PHP version, and filter by application baseline, optional, installed or available entries.
The list combines loaded modules and extension packages from configured repositories for installed runtimes. A package may provide several modules.
Baseline labels identify common WordPress/WHMCS support. Requirements depend on the actual application release and plugins. Do not install every optional extension.
Choose Install only for a required compatible package. The selected PHP-FPM version restarts, affecting its websites. Confirm and verify the application afterwards.
Core modules and installed baseline packages are protected. PHP 7.3 container modules require an image rebuild. Source-only extensions outside configured repositories are not listed.

topics.title: WAF and malware scanning
steps: Optional security engines must be installed before their controls can work.
Start the WAF in Detect mode for a website. Check legitimate traffic and tune false positives before enabling Block.
Run a malware scan for the chosen website/path. Scans report findings; they do not automatically clean or repair application files.
Keep PHP, the OS, WordPress/WHMCS, themes and plugins updated. Security features cannot guarantee a server is unhackable.

topics.title: Manage network rules
steps: Review existing rules before creating or removing a rule. Enter the exact port, protocol, direction, action and source required.
Keep your administrator connection and panel access allowed. Confirm provider/cloud firewalls separately; a panel rule does not change those.
Expose only the services you use. FTP passive ranges and mail ports have separate requirements. Incorrect rules can lock out clients or administrators.

topics.title: Server settings
steps: Set the administrator contact email, time zone and standard-backup retention in Settings. Search the global time-zone list to find the correct region.

The DNS resolver section shows detected default DNS resolvers. With systemd-resolved, these are the live upstreams for ordinary unmatched queries; existing split-domain routes remain unchanged. Conflicting default routes are reported before settings change. The installer enforces 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4. A system check runs after boot and every five minutes; changes to other default resolvers will be restored to these defaults.
Changing the hostname does not update public DNS, mail identity or certificates. Reboot disconnects all hosted services until the server returns.
Change the administrator password using the current password and matching new-password fields. Keep recovery access to the server.

topics.title: Recent Activities
steps: Open System → Recent Activities to see retained event details with pagination. The dashboard also provides recent-event pages.
Forever is the default. Optional retention is 7, 15, 30, 60 or 365 days. Saving a limited period permanently removes older events after confirmation, then applies as new events are recorded.
Delete everything removes recorded activity after confirmation. New activity continues to be recorded. Previously discarded events cannot be recovered.

topics.title: Common problems
steps: Session expired: sign into LiteCP again, then reopen the tool. Panel updates/restarts may end the administrator session.
A new tab did not open: permit new tabs/popups for your LiteCP address, then retry the user action.
SSL request failed: confirm domain DNS points here and HTTP validation can reach this server. Use a certificate matching the hostname; do not disable verification.
Backup/import failed: read the error and verify free space, archive limits, file types and target emptiness. Partial backup/export files may be retained for review.
Website error after a runtime change: check PHP compatibility, required extensions, application configuration and relevant logs.
Mail cannot send/receive: verify MX/A/SPF/DKIM/DMARC/PTR, credentials, TLS, service state, port reachability and provider restrictions.
This manual describes panel capabilities. Optional components may be unavailable until installed; always follow the status and confirmation shown by the live panel.
